lp-py-yaml-unsafe-load.rule:
patterns:
  - pattern: yaml.load(...)
  - pattern-not: yaml.load($S, Loader=yaml.SafeLoader)
  - pattern-not: yaml.load($S, Loader=yaml.CSafeLoader)
  - pattern-not: yaml.load($S, yaml.SafeLoader)
  - pattern-not: yaml.load($S, yaml.CSafeLoader)
lp-py-yaml-unsafe-load.message: yaml.load with the default, full or unsafe loader can build arbitrary Python objects, so a crafted YAML document can run code. Use yaml.safe_load or pass Loader=yaml.SafeLoader.

lp-py-tar-extractall-unfiltered.rule:
patterns:
  - pattern-either:
      - pattern: tarfile.open(...).extractall(...)
      - patterns:
          - pattern-either:
              - pattern-inside: |
                  with tarfile.open(...) as $T:
                    ...
              - pattern-inside: |
                  $T = tarfile.open(...)
                  ...
          - pattern: $T.extractall(...)
  - pattern-not: $X.extractall(..., filter=$F, ...)
lp-py-tar-extractall-unfiltered.message: A tar archive is unpacked with extractall and no extraction filter, so a member named ../x or /etc/x is written outside the target folder. Pass filter="data" (Python 3.12+, backported to 3.8+ security releases).
lp-py-tar-extractall-unfiltered.fixture:
import tarfile
import zipfile


def unpack_release(pkg, target):
    with tarfile.open(pkg, "r:*") as bundle:
        # ruleid: sast.python.lp-py-tar-extractall-unfiltered
        bundle.extractall(target)


def unpack_backup(pkg, target):
    bk = tarfile.open(pkg)
    # ruleid: sast.python.lp-py-tar-extractall-unfiltered
    bk.extractall(target, members=None)


def unpack_inline(pkg):
    # ruleid: sast.python.lp-py-tar-extractall-unfiltered
    tarfile.open(pkg, "r:bz2").extractall("/tmp/x")


def filtered(pkg, target):
    with tarfile.open(pkg) as bundle:
        # ok: sast.python.lp-py-tar-extractall-unfiltered
        bundle.extractall(target, filter="data")


def filtered_inline(pkg):
    # ok: sast.python.lp-py-tar-extractall-unfiltered
    tarfile.open(pkg).extractall("/tmp/y", filter="tar")


def zipped(pkg, target):
    with zipfile.ZipFile(pkg) as z:
        # ok: sast.python.lp-py-tar-extractall-unfiltered
        z.extractall(target)

lp-py-requests-no-timeout.message: Every requests call is flagged (over-broad first draft).

lp-py-requests-no-timeout.rule:
patterns:
  - pattern-either:
      - pattern: requests.get(...)
      - pattern: requests.post(...)
      - pattern: requests.put(...)
  - pattern-not: requests.$M(..., timeout=$T, ...)
lp-py-requests-no-timeout.message: This HTTP call has no timeout, so a slow or silent server can hang the worker indefinitely. Pass timeout= with a sensible number of seconds.

lp-py-subprocess-unchecked.rule:
patterns:
  - pattern: subprocess.run(...)
  - pattern-not: subprocess.run(..., check=True, ...)
lp-py-subprocess-unchecked.message: The command's exit status is ignored, so a failure goes unnoticed. Pass check=True.
lp-py-subprocess-unchecked.fixture:

# ruleid: sast.python.lp-py-subprocess-unchecked

# ruleid: sast.python.lp-py-subprocess-unchecked
subprocess.run(["b"], text=True)
# ruleid: sast.python.lp-py-subprocess-unchecked
subprocess.run(["c"], timeout=1)
# ok: sast.python.lp-py-subprocess-unchecked
subprocess.run(["a"], check=True)
# ok: sast.python.lp-py-subprocess-unchecked
subprocess.run(["b"], text=True, check=True)
# ok: sast.python.lp-py-subprocess-unchecked
subprocess.run(["c"], check=True, timeout=1)
